headline: Costco presented plans for a major warehouse and gas station on Coslin Drive, while committees prepared warrant articles and budgets.
synopsis: The Planning Board opened a public hearing on a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 15-pump fueling facility at 21 Coslin Drive, continuing the review to October 19 amid resident and board questions on traffic and noise. Ahead of Special Town Meeting, the Trails Committee discussed outreach and a potential floor amendment to secure Community Preservation Act funding for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge after receiving unfavorable recommendations from town boards. In addition, the Southborough School Committee launched its FY28 budget process, reviewing town guidelines that mandate level-service and level-funded models while extending its capital outlook to 8 to 10 years.

highlights.title: Costco warehouse and gas station proposal
highlights.why: Costco unveiled site, utility, and traffic plans for a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 15-pump gas station spanning Southborough and Westborough. The board and residents raised concerns over weekend traffic volumes, loading dock noise, and cut-through routes.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge funding strategy
highlights.why: Following non-recommendation votes from the Select Board and Advisory Committee, the committee prepared voter outreach and evaluated a fallback floor amendment reducing new CPA funding requests to $25,000 for Article 4 at Special Town Meeting.

highlights.title: FY28 school budget guidelines and timeline
highlights.why: Administrators presented town budget directives requiring the district to prepare both a level-service budget and a level-funded budget with capped non-salary expenses. Key factors being tracked include special education out-of-district tuitions and potential Neary project transition costs.

highlights.title: Two-family dwelling zoning bylaw warrant article
highlights.why: The Planning Board continued its hearing to Town Meeting morning following discussions about whether current draft language could unintentionally permit two-family homes on smaller commercial lots.

highlights.title: Expanded school capital planning horizon
highlights.why: During a review of FY28 budget priorities, the committee decided to expand its capital planning outlook from five years to an 8-to-10-year window to improve forecasting for major building components such as roofs and HVAC systems.

looking_ahead.what: Multi-board convening on elementary school building options
Second reading of draft budget priorities and capital plan discussion
Pre-Town Meeting continued hearing on two-family dwelling warrant article
